chunks: Muhammad ibn ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) or from Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him), who said:

He forbade the marriage of two women [to one man] where there is no dower for either of them except the sexual intercourse [consummation] of her companion [the other wife], and he said: It is not permissible for him to marry one of the two except with a dower, and [with] the marriage [customs] of the Muslims.

key_terms.شِيهَار: Exchange marriage (implied by context of 'not having a dower except the companion')
key_terms.صَاحِبَتِهَا: Her companion / peer (referring to the other wife in the exchange)

ai.seo_question: What is Shighar marriage and how does it differ from valid marriage regarding dowry?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the prohibition of Shighar, a pre-Islamic practice where two men exchanged daughters without independent dowries, by stipulating that each wife must have her own distinct mahr. It emphasizes that validity requires adherence to the established customs ('urf) of the Muslims, ensuring the transaction is not merely a barter of women. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that while the form of exchange is invalid, the underlying principle of mutual consent and proper compensation remains central to marital contracts.
